html:
The Worimi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the coast of New South Wales around Port Stephens and the Great Lakes. Their country ran from the Hunter River estuary north to Forster.

They speak the Gathang language, a dialect chain shared with the Birrbay to the north. Their other neighbours were the Awabakal around Newcastle and the Wonnarua up the Hunter Valley.

In 1824 the Australian Agricultural Company took a grant of a million acres at Port Stephens for sheep and later cattle, and its men took over Worimi land. Today the Worimi Conservation Lands, which include the great sand dunes of Stockton Bight, are owned by the Worimi people.
